prose_updates.tldr: Announced staggered policies can make one future-treated cohort serve as an anticipatory comparison in several Callaway--Sant'Anna risk sets. Each implementation cohort is attached to one known canonical announcement-and-implementation path, and the reference path has neither event. Over the proposal-specific canonical-path class, PT--All makes the reference-path conditional means additive, preregistered edgewise level boxes bound announcement-to-implementation responses, and bounded support constrains every reference-path cohort--time mean. The admissible anticipation vectors are exactly the primitive box intersected with the fundamental-cycle equations. The resulting theory gives the minimal-face dimension, the bridge frontier for variation independence, negative-cycle endpoint certificates, and min-cost-circulation endpoints for every signed ATT aggregate. A conditional endpoint-mixture construction now proves that every bounded cycle-compatible mean vector extends to one common law of all path potential outcomes, so the affine ATT region and its circulation endpoints are causally sharp rather than conditionally sharp. Simultaneous bounded-mean bands yield finite-sample honest outer confidence sets by one joint optimization. The only transfer to the Callaway--Sant'Anna published setup is the explicit zero-anticipation rectangular-anchor reduction; no inclusion relation with Fenaroli's published class is asserted.

project_justification.gap: Callaway--Sant'Anna not-yet-treated comparisons can reuse future-treated cohorts, but their identification theorem avoids contaminated comparison cells under its limited-anticipation design. Fenaroli's Section 4.2 uses never-treated controls and notes the additional comparison-group anticipation problem. Neither published class supplies joint cycle restrictions for reused contaminated cells or a common-law completion proving sharpness of all overlapping targets at once.
project_justification.niche: A deterministic canonical policy path for each cohort makes anticipation a well-typed path contrast. In the proposal-specific class, PT--All turns the no-announcement mean surface into an incidence potential, edgewise level intervals encode responses between the known announcement and implementation dates, and bounded outcome support becomes a complete bipartite interval-tension restriction. Cycles govern compatibility, bridges govern primitive-coordinate independence, and ATT weights become node demands.
project_justification.fill: The project proves the cycle fiber and its face-correct dimension, necessary and sufficient bridge and endpoint frontiers, a bounded-outcome causal completion theorem, exact affine identified regions, min-cost-circulation endpoint formulas, and finite-sample outer coverage. The completion is constructive: one endpoint-mixture law preserves the entire observed panel and realizes every target simultaneously. The result is exact for the proposal-specific canonical-path, PT--All, edgewise-level-box class. It does not claim to settle the larger or differently restricted classes of Callaway--Sant'Anna or Fenaroli.

prose_updates.related_work: CallawaySantAnna2021, Assumption 3 and Theorem 1, supplies the not-yet-treated aggregation workflow used by applications. The present Proposition~\ref{prop:known-corners} reproduces its familiar two-by-two functional only in the zero-anticipation rectangular-anchor corner; no inclusion of the full Callaway--Sant'Anna class is claimed. Fenaroli2026, Section 4.2, derives staggered bounds using never-treated controls and observes that comparison-group anticipation must be addressed before using not-yet-treated controls. Its cohort-level increment restrictions and this note's edgewise canonical-path level boxes define different classes, so neither class-inclusion direction is asserted. Gong2022 bounds anticipation in classical and staggered difference-in-differences settings without deriving the common cycle restrictions studied here. AugustinGutknechtLiu2025 treats anticipation as timing misspecification and motivates the Indonesian anti-cheating application, using groups known to be unaffected for correction. PiccininniTchetgenStensrud2025 motivates indexing outcomes by complete policy-decision paths rather than implementation dates alone. Torgovitsky2019 emphasizes full-distribution extensions in sharp partial identification; Theorem~\ref{thm:causal-completion} provides the proposal-specific extension directly. Dawid2001 supplies the product-range notion of variation independence, JochmansWeidner2019 the incidence and gauge language for two-way effects, and ChenKyngLiuPengProbstGutenbergSachdeva2022 the general minimum-cost-flow setting. Voronin2025 and FangLiebl2026 address generic linear-program or functional asymptotic inference, whereas the present finite-sample result propagates one simultaneous bounded-mean event through a cycle-coupled region.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The exhaustive early kill test remains computational evidence rather than part of the proof. This solve enumerated all 511 nonempty subgraphs of the three-cohort by three-period bipartite graph and tested two deterministic rational-input instances per graph, including zero-width coordinates and disconnected graphs. Across 1,022 feasibility comparisons, the direct linear program, interval-tension program, and negative-cycle certificate agreed; across all 922 feasible cases, direct support, node-potential support, and split-flow transshipment values agreed to numerical tolerance. The causal completion theorem does not rest on that enumeration; it follows from the explicit endpoint-mixture construction. That construction proves existence and mean sharpness only. Its common latent uniform is one admissible coupling and carries no claim that cross-path dependence, marginal distributions beyond their means and support, or sensitivity magnitudes are identified from the observed law.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The completed result is sharp over \(\mathfrak M(P_{\mathrm{obs}})\): the proposal-specific class of known canonical announcement-and-implementation paths satisfying consistency, PT--All for the no-announcement reference path, preregistered edgewise level bounds on pre-implementation path effects, cohort overlap where conditional targets are used, and bounded potential outcomes. Every feasible \(\beta\in\mathcal Q_Y(\mu)\) is embedded in one common full law, so no target-specific completion or additional cross-path compatibility inequality is needed. This is not the published Callaway--Sant'Anna class and not Fenaroli's published class. The only Callaway--Sant'Anna transfer claimed is the zero-anticipation two-by-two formula under the explicit rectangular anchor \(\mathsf{RA}\); no class inclusion or Fenaroli-class transfer is claimed. The minimal-face formula uses \(\mathcal I(\mu)\) when feasibility forces a proper box face, and finite circulation endpoints require \(\mathcal Q_Y(\mu)\ne\varnothing\). The sensitivity intervals, policy paths, and announcement dates are fixed before outcome analysis. Covariate-conditional extensions, learned sensitivity magnitudes, endogenous or heterogeneous announcements, continuous timing, distributional treatment effects, and uniform optimality of the outer confidence set remain outside scope.
